text: Based on the tool output, the 2021 tree-cover loss in the pine plantation was likely caused by timber harvest. The loss area of 81.3 hectares was observed in 2021 by the Hansen Global Forest Change dataset, and 98% of this area was mapped as forest in 2020 by the JRC Global Forest Cover dataset. The MGAP forest map indicates that the event area was entirely planted forest, specifically Pinus elliottii and Pinus taeda, with no native forest present. Additionally, there was no further loss observed in later years, suggesting that the loss was not due to a disturbance event like a fire or disease. The size and nature of the loss are consistent with timber harvest activities.
